subject: Urgent: FalconBridge VPC throughput collapse — request for emergency tuning & exec sync
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@falconbridge.ai>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: sre@falconbridge.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ACTION REQUIRED] FalconBridge VPC: throughput and latency collapse

Hi Sergio,

We woke up to a significant degradation on our Redwood private deployment in our us-west-2 VPC. Since ~00:30 UTC we've seen sustained throughput drop (~60%) and p95 tail latency increase ~5x for our inference route (model: redwood-mmini-3b-q4f16). Error rates are low 502/504s but timeouts and queueing are present; the customer-facing service is impacted.

I attached capture logs and a brief p95 timeline. Early notes: no infra changes from our side; we rolled a prompt-set change yesterday evening that increased average sequence length by ~40%.

Can Redwood triage and propose an immediate mitigation? We need:
- An engineer on-call for triage now (screenshare)
- Suggested config changes we can apply (batching, kernel profile, KV cache settings)
- If necessary, a short-term plan to route traffic to a less-loaded model variant or temporary reserved nodes

I'm available for a call in 20 minutes.

Attached: support_log_2027-04-19.tar.gz, p95-delta-runbook.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Park
SRE Lead, FalconBridge AI

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@falconbridge.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] FalconBridge VPC: throughput and latency collapse

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're on it.

Immediate plan:
1) Triage call in 15m (I'll start a Zoom + recording) — joining: me (SRE escalation), Karthik (Solutions), Marissa (CS/Account), Laura (Account exec)
2) Quick mitigations to try during call:
   - Pin requests to 8k sequence variant and short-circuit long-streaming calls
   - Reduce batch window to 0.02s and force-request-serialization for hot routes
   - Temporarily enable KV prefix sticky caching (if not already enabled)
3) If those don't recover, Karthik will propose a routing plan to fall back to a smaller model variant (redwood-mmini-3b-int8) on dedicated reserves.

Please join the call here: https://zoom.redwood.com/j/823-942-112 (passcode: falcon1)

Sergio
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, Elena Park <elena.park@falconbridge.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] FalconBridge VPC: throughput and latency collapse

Elena / team — quick hypothesis after a rapid log peek: the prompt-set change that increased average seq length will both increase per-request token compute and expand KV working set. On VPCs with tight memory budgets that can push the runtime into frequent KV evictions -> more cache misses -> increased latency and lower throughput.

What I need now (if you can send):
- full kernels.log from the last 6 hours (I saw a snippet in the tar)
- seq-length distribution (histogram) per route
- sample request header with batching metadata (batch_id, timestamp)

Immediate changes we can push during call (low risk):
- Temporarily restrict max_input_tokens to previous baseline (reduce avg seq)
- Force smaller batching (0.01s) and enable urgent_request_mode for the hot route to prioritize latency over throughput
- If KV churn is the problem, enable sticky-prefix caching and increase per-shard KV retention by +25% (will cost memory)

If we need a fallback: we can route 30% of traffic to mmini-int8 on dedicated reserved nodes in the same region; this gives a predictable p95 while we tune kernels and model config. That requires an approval for short-term reserved capacity (couple hours) and I can stage the rollout from the console.

-Karthik
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@falconbridge.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] FalconBridge VPC: throughput and latency collapse

Thanks — call notes and next steps (recording link posted to Drive): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/FB-FalconBridge/incident-20270419

I've drafted a one-page MOP with rollback criteria and the approval window for routing to dedicated nodes. Sharing here for quick sign-off.

Key asks for FalconBridge:
- Approve temporary change to max_input_tokens to previous baseline (list provided in Drive)
- Approve sticky-prefix caching toggle and +25% KV retention for 90 minutes
- If we roll to dedicated nodes, confirm you accept a short-term capacity charge. We recommend a 3-hour window to cover testing + ramp.

I'll be on the call to coordinate applying the toggles — Sergio / Karthik, pls confirm who will execute each step.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: request for CTO-level awareness and emergency reserved capacity approval

Team — looping in product & finance leadership as this affects a top-tier enterprise account (FalconBridge, deal FB-ENT-2026-09).

Summary: per SRE and Solutions notes, a prompt rollout increased avg seq length which likely caused KV cache churn and p95 surge. Proposed mitigations include config toggles plus a short-term routing of 30% traffic to a smaller model on reserved nodes.

Ask of leadership (please reply to this thread):
- Approve emergency reserved capacity for us-west-2 for up to 3 hours (estimate: $1,200) to be charged to the FalconBridge bill as an emergency capacity action.
- Approve offering a one-time service credit (suggested 7% of last month's invoice) as a good-faith gesture for impact during the incident.

I will schedule a 30-minute exec briefing in 1 hour to review root cause and remediation timeline. We need sign-off within 30 minutes to proceed with routing fallback.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena.park@falconbridge.ai>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 03:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] FalconBridge VPC: throughput and latency collapse

Thanks everyone — we've joined the call and confirmed the first set of toggles (rollback of max_input_tokens and reduced batching) improved p95 by ~35% within 12 minutes. We'll keep the sticky-prefix cache enabled while you validate retention tuning.

FalconBridge approves short-term reserved capacity for the fallback routing. We appreciate the quick response — please proceed and keep us posted on the exec briefing outcomes.

Elena
SRE Lead, FalconBridge AI
